en.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/218498749_4629189100424424_752911054758201723_n.jpg

Psychoanalysts have most often been compared to archaeological excavators who, in addition to theoretical and scientific knowledge, require a certain patience, endurance, perseverance, as well as a rich general culture.

Hassan Makaremi — In the three essays that you will read under the title "Psychoanalysis and Culture", I set out to examine the psychological fields—comprising psychoanalysis, psychiatry, psychology, and psychotherapy—and the role of culture in their theoretical and clinical dimensions.

These three discourses comprise the following sections: an introduction, the four psychological fields of psychoanalysis, the contribution of Sigmund Freud, the contribution of Jacques Lacan, and applied psychoanalysis. In a forthcoming series of articles, I shall also endeavour to address the role and reciprocal influences of research in the humanities, psychology, and psychoanalysis in Iran and the world, as well as their relationship with states and administrative structures.

Introduction: Without addressing the concepts of the psychological and of culture, speaking of psychoanalysis is virtually impossible. For this reason, after a brief discussion of the various fields of knowledge of the psyche, I shall turn concisely to theoretical and clinical psychoanalysis, and at the end I shall dissect the relationship between psychoanalysis and culture. In opening my remarks, and to illuminate what I have to say, it is fitting to examine the correspondence between Einstein and Freud.

In 1932, Albert Einstein, who had the experience of the First World War behind him, expressed his concern over the state of the world in a letter to Sigmund Freud: "Dear Mr Freud, is there any way of delivering humanity from the menace of war? Why must human beings kill one another so ruthlessly? Why have all efforts towards a lasting peace ended in failure? Why are human beings so bloodthirsty and merciless? Why do people allow criminal and mad dictators to exploit their emotions and drive them to the brink of madness and the killing of their neighbours? Is it possible to guide the development of the human psyche in a direction capable of withstanding the madness of hatred and destruction?"

After a discussion on the history of war, Freud turns to analysing his theory and writes: "Human drives are of two kinds: those that seek self-preservation and the unification of life—these are called erotic or sexual drives—and those that seek annihilation and death; we summarise them as the aggressive drive and the destructive drive. It appears that neither of these drives operates in isolation. For instance, when a person falls in love, the instinct of possession, ownership, and aggressiveness is also intensified in them; yet the destructive drive—death and devastation—is active within every living organism and strives gradually to destroy and disintegrate the living being and return life to an inanimate state, whereas the drive of love and desire, which stands at the opposite pole, represents the efforts of life. Our aim is not the total eradication of human beings' aggressive tendencies; we must only try to channel this inclination so that it does not erupt in the form of war. Certainly, the ideal and desirable condition is a society whose people have subjected and subordinated their instinctual life to the sovereignty of reason and intellect.

"One cannot condemn all wars in principle. So long as powers exist that stand ready ruthlessly to annihilate others, others too must arm themselves for war. Among the psychological characteristics of cultural evolution, two features are of great significance: one is the strengthening of the intellect, which gains mastery over instinctual life, and the other is the internalisation of aggressive tendencies, with all its beneficial consequences and all its perilous risks. How long must we wait before the peoples of the world become peace-loving? I do not know. My sole hope lies in the cultural attitude, and the other lies in a justified fear of the effects and consequences of war. Anything that aids cultural evolution, strengthens it, and accelerates it undoubtedly serves positively against war…"

Even in this brief excerpt, the depth and breadth of Freud's vision are evident. In answering Einstein's question, Freud undertakes a profound examination of life and views the history, emergence, and growth of humankind as contemporaneous with the presence of a stratum termed the cultural crystallisation of humanity. Freud points to what returns within the human psyche, which he himself calls the unconscious. It is not for nothing that in 1930 society finally awakened and Freud received the prestigious official Goethe Prize for his collected works—a prize awarded once a year to individuals who have contributed to the enrichment of culture. Yet before long, Freud's works in Germany suffered the fiery fate of the books of Marx, Bertolt Brecht, and others.

Freud holds that through the elevation of human culture, one can wage war against war. In his theory, he draws upon the concept of sublimation, or "cultural elevation" (*bâlâ bar shodan-e farhangi*). I have employed the phrase "elevation" in preference to the technical Arabic-derived word *tasâ'od*, because the term *sublimation* denotes rising to a higher state both in its scientific usage in chemistry and allied sciences and in clinical psychoanalysis.

Moreover, the Persian word *farhang* (culture) itself conveys the notion of the elevation of knowledge: *farhang* is formed from the prefix *far*, meaning splendour, stature, and loftiness, and *hang*, meaning gravity, dignity, power, capability, vigour, and strength—signifying a lofty and elevated power and capability.

Freud first made use of this term to show that across the various stages of the psychoanalytic journey, the individual attains a stage of "elevation" (sublimation), such that bodily needs—sexual, alimentary, and the like—give way to higher (psychic) needs, or cultural ones in all their dimensions. Yet what can the role of cultural elevation be in the realm of art?

What does the ear of the clinical psychoanalyst hear from the enraptured gaze? The artist asks: "Do you like it? It is my work." What relationship exists between a work of art and cultural sublimation? The impulses that regulate our psychic life arise from a source, flow towards an aim, and persist until the satisfaction of their productive roots. When these bodily impulses rising from our physique towards our psyche reach maturity, they alter their aim. The aim is placed on a plane higher than the body, and the satisfaction of the need transcends everyday bodily life. These messages seek a new "place" in order to present a new message, and perhaps a new discovery. Put differently, this "higher aim" demands other words and other concepts.

Examples abound. In his works, Picasso in a sense reconstructs the gaze of primeval human beings upon themselves and upon existence. In the faces he fashions, whether in drawing or in sculpture, Picasso seems to revive that ancestral gaze upon himself and other people. It is as though he has found that "new place". Salvador Dalí displays in his works the magic of colourful and wondrous dreams. Before him, it seemed scarcely conceivable that a human being could be so much a magician in his dreams—dreams that lay before our eyes time and space just as they pass in sleep, like the dream itself. Upon leaving an exhibition of his works, it feels as though we are waking from a sweet, enchanting slumber.

Van Gogh draws that inner force of the real world onto his canvases. Everything—a table, a flower, a tree, a shirt—radiates life force. In his works, the union of matter and energy meets the eye. Goya, the Spanish painter of so many brilliant works, begins with court life, collective hunts, and the beauty of natural scenes; then, in his celebrated work *The Executions* (*El tres de mayo*), without even painting the eyes of the man facing the firing squad, he shows us his "gaze". Look closely: in place of this man's eyes, Goya has placed only two black smudges. His supreme art lies precisely in this "placement"—a gaze suspended between death and life through two black smudges.

In dissecting the phenomenon of "cultural elevation", Sigmund Freud states that it is an activity rooted in sexuality yet emptied of it. This energy passes through narcissism and moves towards the ego ideal, or the ultimate "I". Bodily needs ascend and journey towards that ultimate figure which the "I" has nurtured in its imagination. This "I" is the object of our longing, out of reach, whom we would attain in a state of perfection of the self—and undoubtedly such a being exists in imagination, not in reality. It is as though the body and its needs give way, in two stages, to narcissism and then to a higher, ultimate fascination, like the experience of Narcissus who falls in love with his own reflection in the water. This mirror image of the "I" places the artist, in a way, in the position of a camera, and his work, like a photograph, is the product of this camera—just as the quality of the photograph speaks to the quality of the camera. Thus narcissism signifies the ennobling and elevation of the productions of this "I".

This is perhaps what is "metaphorically" inscribed in the smile of Leonardo da Vinci's *Mona Lisa*. That narcissism of the artist upon sublimation was perhaps, before the rise of modern artists in the visual arts prior to our era, the perfection of art through depicting the external world as realistically as possible—a kind of perfecting of the camera. Here, the artist's unconscious image of his own body is directly laid bare to view: the answer the artist gives to the unending question, "What am I like?"

The Four Psychological Fields

The complexities of the psyche and their domains of operation—very briefly and in passing: psychoanalysis, psychiatry, psychology, and psychotherapy. What pertains to the psychological field may be presented thus: the use of the word *ravân* (psyche/soul) in Persian as the equivalent of "PSY" in European languages may be regarded as a blessing of the Persian language. For this word can both denote the concept of the "psychic apparatus"—or the structure of the psyche's functioning—and serve as a suffix or prefix for all concepts that deal in any way with the psyche, among them *ravân-kâvi* (psychoanalysis), *ravân-shenâsi* (psychology), *ravân-pezeshki* (psychiatry), *ravân-darmâni* (psychotherapy), or *ravân-shenâkhti* (psychological). Indeed, the word *ravân*, which is at the same time the verbal noun of the verb *raftan* ("to go", "to flow"), conveys this relationship through the very fluidity of the concept of "psyche"—such that the psyche is at once within us, with us, and elsewhere. In Iranian myths, this place is a kind of celestial earth, and in the modern hypotheses of Lacanian psychoanalysis it is the other, the Big Other, or others.

Although the complexities of the human psyche are not the subject solely of the sciences in the modern sense, what has been formally defined within the scientific scope of the psychological circle may be divided into four groups: psychiatry, psychology, psychotherapy, and psychoanalysis. This provisional classification enables us, in this brief survey, to become better acquainted with the psychological field of operation. Let us call knowledge pertaining to the psyche "psychological", on the assumption that we restrict our field of work to everyday life and the tangible realm. For the domain of knowledge of the psyche reaches back, on one side, to the study of all human achievements—from the invention of speech and writing to mythology, art, and literature, from the remotest times to the present day; within this span lie philosophy, mysticism, religion, folk beliefs, charm-writing, and magic as well. On the other side, without venturing too far afield, the psychological extends to linguistics, anthropology, and sociology; and because the psyche rests upon the body, the psychological advances into neurology. In fact, the human psyche is caught amid three major coordinates: the human past, the human being among the collectivity of others, and the human body with its nervous structure.

Let us try to clarify the matter by defining the four concepts of practical psychological application and offering a few examples:

1. Psychiatry, which historically lies within the scope of medicine and is a branch continuing from medicine of the brain and nerves. In psychiatry, we deal with the classification of illnesses based on their external manifestations. The aim is the diagnosis and treatment of illness. Mental illnesses within the domain of psychiatry may derive their roots in some way from the body, the nervous system, or impaired brain function—illnesses rooted in congenital factors or difficulties arising after birth, such as brain lesions, malfunctioning of the memory system, the discernment system, or cognitive structure. In treating disorders today, psychiatry investigates somatic-neurological causes, employs everything from psychotherapy to environmental change, art therapy, and so forth, and assigns a special role to chemical medications in calming the patient's mental space. In the early twentieth century, the departments of nervous diseases, brain medicine, and psychiatry were not yet separated from one another.

2. In psychology, the behaviour of the individual is analysed—the individual's behaviour in the family, educational setting, workplace, and with friends and acquaintances. Hence this science is used wherever "individual behaviour" plays a role, such as recruitment in institutions, public relations, educational sciences, or regulating the individual's relationship with others or within the social environment. In clinical settings, psychology places the individual before a mirror of their behaviour towards society and others. Psychology plays a major role in the rehabilitation of individuals who, owing to congenital deficiency or accidents and illnesses, suffer from behavioural or mental disorders. Another major activity of psychology lies in all research areas linked to cognitive sciences and behavioural sciences; moreover, studying social issues is impractical without considering the individual's behaviour towards society (social psychology)—psychology is highly effective through group work in reactivating patients' mental faculties.

3. Psychotherapy. Backed by experience and using dialogue, psychotherapy seeks to confront the individual locally with their specific disorder and guide them towards an acceptable solution. In certain cases (and when necessary), psychiatrists draw upon psychotherapy to resolve disorders such as anxieties, temporary disorientation, or passing distress.

4. Psychoanalysis is a recent practice with a history of less than a century. Psychoanalysis attends to the individual's speech on the couch. The psychoanalyst operates in the individual's relationship with their unconscious, and their field of action is akin to placing a mirror before the individual's speech so that, by this means and over the long term (typically between five and ten years), through recounting whatever comes to mind (free association), the individual gains awareness of how their unconscious operates and thereby reaches the root of possible behavioural disorders. Many disorders are "resolved" in recognising their root. On the other hand, psychoanalysis assists in discovering the individual's latent inner strengths, and today this is one of the most important uses of psychoanalysis in Western societies—as a kind of preparation to move in a new direction with a deeper knowledge of one's weaknesses and strengths, like a sailor who, by sharpening his vision, steers his ship better through the storm.

Psychoanalytic training is most often likened to a master–apprentice transmission. For if the psychoanalyst has not personally passed through the couch and undertaken psychic exploration—or unearthed the roots of their own "unconscious"—how could they guide another person? In psychoanalysis, we encounter two phenomena: clinical psychoanalysis and applied psychoanalysis. On the basis of psychoanalytic theories, one can examine writings, speeches, and works of art, opening a new angle on the method of analysing and interpreting art and literature. For this reason, today in many educational establishments, universities, and research centres, psychoanalysts serve as members of research teams.

Let us take an example: consider the daily life of a family—Mr and Mrs "M" and their two children, the elder and the younger. Mr M's father suffers from amnesia; under the supervision of a specialist psychologist, he strives to combat this difficulty with exercises three days a week.

Mrs M, for the past four years, following the appearance of neurotic symptoms—a groundless and constant fear—has been undergoing psychoanalytic treatment; she sees her psychoanalyst three times a week, and practically her time is spent on the couch speaking whatever enters her mind. The first child, twenty years old with a mental age of eight, suffers from intellectual disability; a psychologist monitors him and keeps in touch with his instructors. Mr M, in order to overcome alcohol addiction, sees his psychotherapist twice a week so as to pass through the difficult stage of withdrawal through dialogue and "verbal" support.

The second child, aged fifteen, experiences difficulty in writing words. His school psychologist is assessing him in order to refer him to the neurology and psychiatry department for more thorough tests, so as to ensure that the root of his difficulty does not lie in the nervous organs. We see how the individual, body, psyche, and surrounding environment form a complex whole in which, at every stage of disorders and difficulties, we require a distinct expertise.

How can one attain expertise in the aforementioned fields today? To answer this question, it is helpful to divide the psychological domains into theoretical-research, clinical, and behavioural subfields. The psychiatrist is active in both the research and clinical domains. The psychologist is active in all three domains, with the distinction that at the clinical stage they require collaboration with a psychiatrist. The psychotherapist has no role in the research and behavioural domains and addresses psychological disorders only locally. The psychoanalyst is practically active in the clinical domain, and their role in the behavioural and research domains rests primarily on transmitting clinical experience. The psychoanalyst works on the unconscious structure of the individual, with long-term outcomes.

Psychoanalysts have most often been compared to archaeological excavators who, in addition to theoretical and scientific knowledge, require a certain patience, endurance, perseverance, as well as a rich general culture. The relationship of psychoanalysis, psychiatrists, psychologists, and psychotherapists with administrative and healthcare bodies and institutions is not uniform across different societies. By way of example, in Germany psychoanalysis is covered by health insurance services. In the United States, numerous institutions conduct psychoanalytic research alongside official medical teaching and research institutions. Whereas in France, for instance, not only is psychoanalysis excluded from health insurance coverage, but existing research institutes can be counted on the fingers of one hand.

Analytical psychology: Followers of Jung who, relying on the concept of the human being and their symbols and believing in the presence of a kind of collective unconscious, endeavour—through recalling dreams and interpreting symbols associated with humankind—to probe, in a sense, the innermost depths of interiority.

Sexology: Sexology, which in practice is called sex therapy, addresses disorders of sexual behaviour and, beyond the physiological aspect, attributes the bulk of functioning to the psyche and culture, on the premise that human sexual behaviour biologically mirrors that of humanity's ancient primate cousins, and all this diversity, variety, and richness of sexual relations is the product of hundreds of thousands of years of human cultural labour. Consequently, most difficulties and disorders are rooted in the psyche and culture. Sigmund Freud is sometimes recognised as one of the founders of sexology.

Dr Hassan Makaremi

Paris, Autumn 2012 (1391)

fr.body_markdown:
Texte de mon érudit ami Monsieur Manouchehr Taghavi Bayat :

*Ceux qui croient au fusil seront anéantis*

*car il existe des gens qui possèdent des fusils meilleurs et plus efficaces.*

*Les fusils détruisent d'autres fusils.*

*Mais un peuple qui pense et fait preuve de sagesse*

*avancera de jour en jour vers le bonheur*

*si d'autres ont de meilleures idées, nous apprenons d'eux, car les idées*

*ne se détruisent pas les unes les autres, mais se fortifient mutuellement.*

*Revenons à la rationalité et à la réflexion…*

*L'histoire du chef libérateur de la France et*

*une grande leçon politique*

Le général Charles de Gaulle fut le chef libérateur de la France durant la Seconde Guerre mondiale. Après la guerre, il accéda à la présidence de la République et, outre les efforts qu'il déploya pour libérer la France de l'occupation de l'Allemagne nazie,

l'une de ses actions les plus notables fut la décolonisation de douze colonies africaines de la France.

En 1969, il organisa un référendum portant sur des réformes juridiques et sociales.

De Gaulle soutenait que, pour remédier aux problèmes dont les vastes protestations de 1968 avaient été l'un des signes, le président de la République avait besoin de pouvoirs et de prérogatives accrus.

Le peuple français, malgré le respect qu'il portait à Charles de Gaulle et qu'il continue de lui porter aujourd'hui, vota « non » à ce référendum, et de Gaulle, n'ayant pas réussi à obtenir la confiance et l'assentiment du peuple,

se retira du pouvoir.

*La grande leçon du peuple français pour les peuples du monde fut celle-ci :*

*les états de service, le sacrifice et le dévouement d'un héros*

*ne constituent pas une justification suffisante pour remettre le destin et la vie d'une nation entre les mains de ce héros.*

*Car cela offre aisément au héros la possibilité de devenir un monstre.*

*La démocratie implique l'égalité des membres de la société et la soumission du gouvernant à la nation ; aucun dirigeant charismatique ne doit recevoir le pouvoir d'imposer sa volonté à la nation.*

La démocratie ne consiste pas à pouvoir, par le vote du peuple,

nommer quelqu'un à une fonction,

mais bien à pouvoir, par le vote du peuple, destituer celui qui occupe le siège du pouvoir.

Dans une société jouissant de la démocratie,

*nul, dans aucun système, ne doit acquérir sur la nation des prérogatives qu'on ne pourrait ensuite lui reprendre autrement que par la guerre et la contrainte.*

*Aucune vertu — fût-ce le patriotisme, le dévouement, la probité ou un passé irréprochable — ne garantit qu'une personne ne sacrifiera pas son propre intérêt ou celui de sa caste et de son groupe sur l'autel de la vérité ou du peuple.*

*Le pouvoir doit donc être limité, temporaire, contrôlable et révocable.*

*C'est là un fil conducteur qui, s'il vient à se perdre dans une société, transforme la vie en prison et en enfer, et chaque fois une nouvelle promesse de délivrance et de salut nous entraîne à sa suite, jusqu'au jour où nous puissions nous sauver de l'enfer que nous avons nous-mêmes bâti.*

Si, en 1969, le peuple avait voté selon le vœu du général de Gaulle, celui-ci serait probablement devenu aujourd'hui un personnage profondément haï, à l'instar du général Franco, de Mouammar Kadhafi, de Mugabe, de Saddam Hussein…

Et de Gaulle serait demeuré président à vie, et jamais, sans guerre civile, révolution ni soulèvement, il n'aurait été possible, au terme de son règne, de lui reprendre le pouvoir pour le transmettre à un autre élu — à plus forte raison de poursuivre en justice un président délinquant ou criminel.

*Tirer les leçons de l'histoire est la condition de la sagesse, et le châtiment de ne point en tirer leçon est la répétition de tous les malheurs de l'histoire.*

en.title: Those Who Believe in the Gun Shall Be Destroyed
en.executive_summary: A text by our erudite friend Mr Manouchehr Taghavi-Bayat: Those who believe in the gun shall be destroyed, for there are always others who possess better and more effective guns. Guns destroy other guns. Yet a people endowed with thought and wisdom shall advance day by day towards happiness, if…
en.body_markdown:
A text by our erudite friend Mr Manouchehr Taghavi-Bayat:

*Those who believe in the gun shall be destroyed,*

*for there are always others who possess better and more effective guns.*

*Guns destroy other guns.*

*Yet a people endowed with thought and wisdom*

*shall advance day by day towards happiness*

*if, when others hold better ideas, we learn from them—for ideas*

*do not destroy one another; rather, they strengthen one another.*

*Let us return to reason and reflection.....*

*The story of the liberating leader of France and*

*a great political lesson*

General Charles de Gaulle was the liberating leader of France during the Second World War. After the war, he rose to the presidency and, beyond his efforts to liberate France from the occupation of Nazi Germany,

among his valuable achievements was the liberation of twelve French colonies in Africa.

In 1969, he held a referendum for legal and social reforms.

De Gaulle claimed that in order to resolve the problems of which the widespread protests of 1968 were one symptom, the president required greater power and authority.

The people of France, despite the respect they held—and still hold—for Charles de Gaulle, voted "no" in that referendum, and de Gaulle, having failed to win the trust and consent of the people,

stepped down from power.

*The great lesson of the people of France for the peoples of the world was that*

*a hero's record of self-sacrifice and service*

*is not sufficient justification for entrusting the destiny and life of a nation into that hero's hands,*

*because it all too easily grants the hero the possibility of becoming a monster.*

*Democracy presupposes the equality of all members of society and the subordination of the ruler to the nation; no charismatic ruler should ever acquire the authority to impose his will upon the nation.*

Democracy is not merely the ability to appoint someone

to high office by popular vote;

rather, democracy is the ability to remove the person sitting in the seat of power through the vote of the people.

In a society blessed with democracy,

*no one, in any system, must ever acquire powers over the nation that can subsequently be reclaimed only by war and coercion.*

*No virtue—not even patriotism, self-sacrifice, integrity, or a distinguished past—guarantees that a person will sacrifice his own interests, or those of his faction and group, for the sake of truth or for the sake of the people.*

*Therefore, power must be limited, temporary, accountable, and revocable.*

*This is the guiding thread which, if lost in any society, turns life into a prison and a hell, and time after time draws us after some new promise of deliverance and salvation, until the day comes when we might rescue ourselves from the hell of our own making.*

Had the people voted in 1969 according to General de Gaulle's wishes, today de Gaulle would most likely have become a deeply reviled figure, akin to General Franco, Muammar Gaddafi, Mugabe, Saddam Hussein...

And de Gaulle would have remained president for the rest of his life; never, without civil war, revolution, or uprising, could power have been taken from him at the end of a term of rule and transferred to another elected representative—still less could a criminal or felonious president ever have been brought to justice.

*Learning from history is the prerequisite of wisdom, and the penalty for failing to learn is the repetition of all the calamities of history.*

fr.title: Déclaration des militants des droits de l'enfant sur les événements du Khouzestan
fr.executive_summary: https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/67657498798798787633.jpg Un collectif de militants œuvrant dans le domaine de l'enfance a publié une déclaration au sujet des événements du Khouzestan, qualifiant ces incidents de déplorables. fr.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/67657498798798787633.jpg

Un collectif de militants œuvrant dans le domaine de l'enfance a publié une déclaration au sujet des événements du Khouzestan, qualifiant ces incidents de déplorables.

Selon le rapport reçu par Ensaf News, voici le texte intégral de cette déclaration accompagné de la liste de ses signataires :

Aux responsables et planificateurs du pays,

Les enfants et les adolescents d'Iran sont les bâtisseurs de l'avenir de cette terre.

Les événements qui frappent aujourd'hui les enfants et les adolescents vulnérables au Khouzestan et dans d'autres régions de ce pays n'auront, pour eux et pour la chère nation iranienne, d'autre conséquence que d'institutionnaliser la violence et l'esprit de vengeance.

Votre premier devoir est de préserver les droits des enfants et des adolescents et de préparer les conditions de leur épanouissement, de leur santé et de leur bien-être. La génération née dans le climat des huit années de la guerre imposée par l'Irak à l'Iran aurait dû, grâce à la reconstruction des villes dévastées, retrouver sa joie de vivre afin de participer à l'édification de ses cités.

Malheureusement, plus de trois décennies après la fin de la guerre Iran-Irak, les mesures nécessaires pour reconstruire les zones sinistrées par la guerre et raviver l'élan vital parmi les habitants de ces régions n'ont non seulement jamais dépassé le stade des slogans, mais, par l'absence de planification et des décisions erronées, la reconstruction des infrastructures essentielles destinées à répondre aux besoins vitaux des populations des provinces méridionales du pays n'a pas non plus été réalisée.

La destruction de l'environnement et de l'écosystème du Khouzestan, cette terre fertile et cœur battant de l'Iran, a entraîné des dommages irréparables et a contraint une population à bout de souffle ainsi que des mères et des pères inquiets pour l'avenir de leurs chers enfants à descendre dans la rue.

Malgré les avertissements répétés des organisations civiques dévouées et leur offre de participer aux programmes de reconstruction des régions touchées par la guerre, aucun signe d'écoute ni de réponse n'a été observé à ce jour chez les exécutants et les décideurs politiques.

Avec une telle approche, il ne faudra pas longtemps avant que nous soyons confrontés à une vague de migration d'enfants et d'adolescents vers les grandes villes telles qu'Ispahan, Chiraz, Machhad, Téhéran et ailleurs, et que nous assistions de plus en plus à la multiplication des enfants et adolescents des rues sans abri, fouillant les ordures, toxicomanes, ainsi qu'à l'extension de la vie dans les bidonvilles périphériques.

Nous avons la certitude que la poursuite de méthodes fondées sur la brutalité et l'accumulation incontrôlable de diverses formes d'anomie sociale finiront tôt ou tard par embraser l'ensemble de la société iranienne.

Au vu des événements de ces derniers jours dans la province la plus fertile du pays, notre cher Khouzestan, nous, signataires de cette déclaration, en tant que collectif d'organisations et de militants de la société civile engagés auprès des enfants et des adolescents, vous demandons instamment, à vous responsables et planificateurs du pays, de bien vouloir sans plus tarder :

Au lieu d'exercer la violence, prêter attention aux revendications légitimes du peuple héroïque du Khouzestan et à l'avenir de ses enfants et adolescents, et consacrer les moyens financiers et le capital humain du pays, par une planification spécialisée, cohérente et scientifique, à la restauration de l'environnement, à l'amélioration des conditions de vie et à la satisfaction des besoins fondamentaux de la population de cette province ;

Par une action urgente et vitale, sauver les enfants et les adolescents des effets destructeurs de la crise et, au lieu de répéter des voies erronées et non scientifiques déjà empruntées, recourir, grâce à une planification coordonnée, à la coopération des organisations populaires et à la participation des populations locales pour reconstruire et bâtir leur avenir.

Les enfants, les adolescents, les familles et l'ensemble du peuple iranien considèrent comme l'un de leurs droits fondamentaux le fait de vivre dans la dignité et la sécurité sur leur terre glorieuse, et cette aspiration ne saurait se réaliser sans la préservation de leur dignité et la garantie de leur bien-être par les responsables et les dirigeants du pays.

en.title: Statement by Child-Rights Activists on the Events in Khuzestan
en.executive_summary: https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/67657498798798787633.jpg A group of activists working in the field of childhood have issued a statement regarding the events in Khuzestan, describing these incidents as regrettable. According to a report received by Ensaf News, the full text of this statement, together with the names of its signatories, follows:…
en.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/67657498798798787633.jpg

A group of activists working in the field of childhood have issued a statement regarding the events in Khuzestan, describing these incidents as regrettable.

According to a report received by Ensaf News, the full text of this statement, together with the names of its signatories, follows:

To the Authorities and Planners of the Country,

The children and adolescents of Iran are the builders of this land's future.

The events unfolding today against vulnerable children and adolescents in Khuzestan and other parts of this country will have no outcome for them and for the dear nation of Iran other than institutionalising violence and a spirit of vengeance.

Your foremost duty is to safeguard the rights of children and adolescents and to prepare the foundations for their growth, health, and welfare. The generation born amidst the eight-year imposed war between Iraq and Iran ought, through the reconstruction of the devastated cities, to have regained its vitality so as to participate in the rebuilding of its towns.

Regrettably, more than three decades after the end of the Iran-Iraq war, the measures required to reconstruct the war-stricken regions and rekindle a zest for life among the inhabitants of these areas have not only failed to move beyond the level of slogans, but owing to a lack of planning and misguided decisions, the reconstruction of essential infrastructure to meet the basic needs of the people in the southern provinces of the country has likewise not been realised.

The destruction of the environment and ecosystem of Khuzestan—that fertile region and beating heart of Iran—has inflicted irreparable damage and driven an exhausted populace, alongside mothers and fathers anxious for the future of their beloved children, onto the streets.

Despite repeated warnings from dedicated civil-society organisations and their declared willingness to participate in reconstruction programmes for the war-damaged areas, no sign of responsiveness or action has thus far been observed among executives and policymakers.

With such an approach, it will not be long before we face a tide of migration of children and adolescents to major cities such as Isfahan, Shiraz, Mashhad, Tehran, and elsewhere, and increasingly witness unprotected street children and adolescents, waste-pickers, substance addiction, and the spread of life in informal settlements.

We are certain that the continuation of violent methods and the uncontrollable accumulation of diverse forms of social pathology will sooner or later engulf the entirety of Iranian society.

Witnessing the events of recent days in the most fertile province of the country, our dear Khuzestan, we, the signatories of this statement, as a collective of civil-society organisations and activists in the field of children and adolescents, call upon you, the authorities and planners of the country, with the utmost urgency:

Instead of resorting to violence, heed the rightful demands of the heroic people of Khuzestan and the future of their children and adolescents, and devote the country's financial resources and human capital, through specialised, coherent, and scientific planning, to restoring the environment, improving livelihoods, and meeting the basic needs of the people of that province;

In an immediate and vital measure, rescue children and adolescents from the destructive effects of the crisis, and instead of repeating misguided and unscientific paths already taken, draw upon coordinated planning, the cooperation of grassroots organisations, and the participation of local communities in rebuilding and shaping their future.

Children, adolescents, families, and the general public of Iran regard living with dignity and security in their proud homeland as one of their fundamental rights, and this aspiration will never be realised without upholding their dignity and ensuring their welfare on the part of the country's authorities and executives.

fr.title: À la mémoire d'Esmaïl Khoï
fr.executive_summary: https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/19068099910220815707729671277194309190031369n.jpg Esmaïl Khoï, poète contemporain et membre de l'Association des écrivains d'Iran, s'est éteint il y a quelques heures à l'âge de 83 ans (né le 30 juin 1938 à Machhad, décédé le 25 mai 2021 à Londres). Que sa chère mémoire…
fr.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/190680999_10220815707729671_277194309190031369_n.jpg

Esmaïl Khoï, poète contemporain et membre de l'Association des écrivains d'Iran, s'est éteint il y a quelques heures à l'âge de 83 ans (né le 30 juin 1938 à Machhad, décédé le 25 mai 2021 à Londres). Que sa chère mémoire demeure honorée.

Nos condoléances à sa fille Saba,

Nous présentons nos condoléances à la famille d'Esmaïl Khoï, à la communauté artistique et culturelle iranienne au sein de l'Association des écrivains d'Iran « en exil » et du PEN Club d'Iran « en exil », ainsi qu'à tous ceux qui l'aimaient.

[https://m.soundcloud.com/khordadesabz/no0accftn5xz](https://m.soundcloud.com/khordadesabz/no0accftn5xz?fbclid=IwAR2z4pf4lWwb79PX_4BefKozwv3mxeZBUcvPHxuSfsX_TmHrA5n8NdPGlcc)

Esmaïl Khoï avait été hospitalisé le vendredi 21 mai en raison d'une grave pneumonie. Malheureusement, l'insuffisance pulmonaire, cardiaque et rénale avait fini par atteindre un stade ne permettant plus aucun traitement.

Et aujourd'hui, nous avons perdu notre cher et précieux poète.

Les poèmes de Khoï ont été traduits dans divers pays en anglais, russe, français, allemand, hindi et ukrainien. Maîtrisant parfaitement la langue anglaise, il a également composé des poèmes en anglais et fut le premier poète iranien à remporter le prix Rückert à Cobourg en 2010.

Après la révolution de 1979, Khoï vécut un temps dans la clandestinité avant de quitter l'Iran en 1984 ; il résidait depuis lors à Londres. Il comptait parmi les fondateurs du PEN Club en exil ainsi que de l'Association des écrivains d'Iran en exil. Depuis la révolution de 1979, il demeura constamment un opposant au régime de la République islamique.

Parmi ses œuvres figurent notamment *Bi-Tab* (*Impatient*), *Az Seday-e Sokhan-e Eshgh* (*De la voix du Verbe d'amour*), *Dar Nabehangam* (*Dans l'intempestif*), *Jahan-e Digari Miafarin-am* (*Je crée un autre monde*) et *Ghahghah-e Nashenidani-ye Marg* (*L'inaudible éclat de rire de la mort*).

Quelques quatrains tirés du recueil *Le Massacre de 1988 à haute voix* (*Koshtar-e 67 be Bang-e Boland*) d'Esmaïl Khoï :

Je ne te dirai point ni quoi ni comment écrire.

De l'état intérieur ou du dehors, écris.

Écris ce qui jaillit du tréfonds de ton cœur,

Ô poète du massacre, avec du sang écris.

Je porte en mon cœur une peine millénaire.

Puissé-je ne plus voir d'autre chagrin du cœur.

Je suis plus vieux de mille ans aujourd'hui,

Avec la brûlure de milliers de jeunes gens sur le cœur.

Avec tout ce sang qui s'est écoulé de son corps,

La force et la vigueur ont quitté les membres de la patrie.

Pourtant, attends que soit arrachée de sa place

Par le torrent renverseur de cheikhs la marée des jeunes vies.

Lorsque monta au pouvoir ce dragon-porc,

Cent fois pire en sa conduite que tous les rois,

La chaîne de notre existence devint

Deuil après deuil après deuil après deuil.

Un cheikh dont la tête est emplie d'ignorance et de superstition,

Dont l'art est le massacre de l'élite de la jeunesse,

Sape nos racines avec sa prière comme une cognée :

Puisse sa propre prière lui briser les reins !

Le juge en quête de prétexte lui posa la question :

— « Accomplis-tu ta prière en toute circonstance ? »

Il ne dit mot, et le juge le fit exécuter :

Ignorant qu'il était musulman, mais sourd et muet.

— « Te lèves-tu pour la prière ? »

— « Jour et nuit, avec ferveur ! »

— « Maudis-tu ton groupuscule ? »

— « D'une malédiction toute particulière ! »

Il vomit pourtant à la question : « Tes compagnons,

Es-tu prêt aussi à leur tirer le coup de grâce ? »

Ô amoureux de l'humain ! Qu'as-tu besoin de ta prière ?

Debout ! Lève la tête, tel le Messie, vers les hauteurs.

Tant ton amour pour le peuple est divin,

Que la prière elle-même devrait s'incliner devant toi en prière.

Ce supplicié qui dort sur le sol de la prison,

Avec la tulipe qui s'est épanouie sur sa poitrine,

Aux dirigeants du parti de la haine, du deuil et de la mort,

Parlait d'amour, d'allégresse et de vie.

Ce supplicié qui gît étendu sur la terre

— Depuis que son chemin l'a mené à Evin —

Était le héraut de la liberté, mais

Est tombé aux mains des hérauts de la religion.

Ce supplicié a reçu sept ou huit balles, mais

C'est par le coup de grâce qu'il a rendu l'âme, mais

Le sourire aux lèvres : car il a fait ses aveux,

Sans livrer le nom d'aucun de ses camarades, mais.

Ce supplicié ne voulait que personne ne fût tué ;

Ni que la main de quiconque fût souillée de sang :

Vois sa bonne fortune ! Il s'est effondré avant

Que de tels monceaux de corps ne s'entassent sur des monceaux.

Ce supplicié portait un cœur semblable aux grands cœurs :

Prêt à se jeter dans la grande mer :

La grande mer de la mort l'a englouti, mais

De lui demeure vivante l'espérance d'un lendemain meilleur.

.

Esmaïl Khoï est né le 30 juin 1938 (9 Tir 1317) à Machhad. Son père jouissait d'une bonne situation financière, mais il s'endetta soudainement et perdit tous ses biens ; alors âgé de huit ans seulement, Esmaïl dut travailler au bazar durant les étés pour subvenir aux besoins quotidiens. Khoï fut un enfant travailleur, mais grâce au soutien de son oncle maternel, il parvint à poursuivre ses études. Après avoir obtenu son diplôme de l'École normale supérieure de Téhéran (Daneshsaray-e Ali), il partit en Grande-Bretagne grâce à une bourse d'études et obtint un doctorat en philosophie à l'Université de Londres. À son retour en Iran, il s'installa à Téhéran et enseigna à l'Université de formation des maîtres de Téhéran (Tarbiat Moallem). Dans un entretien, Khoï raconta avoir été profondément marqué à Téhéran par *L'Hiver* (*Zemestan*) de Mehdi Akhavan-Sales : « Le livre *Zemestan* m'a réveillé et fut la clé de ma rencontre avec la poésie moderne. C'est avec *Zemestan* que je me suis éveillé du sommeil millénaire de la poésie traditionnelle ; après Akhavan, c'est d'abord et avant tout Shamlou que j'ai découvert, puis progressivement d'autres poètes. Nima Youshij fut le dernier des poètes modernistes que j'ai connu à cette époque. » Esmaïl Khoï est l'un des fondateurs de l'Association des écrivains d'Iran et siégea également durant deux mandats au sein de son comité exécutif. De nombreux recueils de poèmes ont été publiés par ses soins, parmi lesquels *Sur le coursier de la terre* (*Bar Kheng-e Rahvar-e Zamin*, 1967), *Sur le toit du tourbillon* (*Bar Bam-e Gerdbad*, 1970), *De la voix du Verbe d'amour* (*Az Seday-e Sokhan-e Eshgh*, 1970), *Au-delà de la nuit des contemporains* (*Faratar az Shab-e Aknounian*, 1971), *Dans l'intempestif* (*Dar Nabehangam*, 1984), *La Proposition du millénaire* (*Gozareh-ye Hezareh*, 1991), *Je crée un autre monde* (*Jahan-e Digari Miafarin-am*, 2000) et *Je suis le poète de mon peuple, la bouche de ma patrie* (*Sha'er-e Khalgham, Dahan-e Mihanam*, 2000) comptent parmi ses œuvres majeures. Le plus récent recueil poétique d'Esmaïl Khoï, intitulé *Mon cœur ne tarde pas* (*Dir Nemishavad Delam*), avait été publié peu avant la mort du poète par les éditions Zagros à Atlanta, aux États-Unis.

en.title: In Memory of Esmail Khoi
en.executive_summary: https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/19068099910220815707729671277194309190031369n.jpg Esmail Khoi, contemporary poet and member of the Iranian Writers' Association, passed away a few hours ago at the age of 83 (born 30 June 1938 in Mashhad; died 25 May 2021 in London). May his dear memory…
en.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/190680999_10220815707729671_277194309190031369_n.jpg

Esmail Khoi, contemporary poet and member of the Iranian Writers' Association, passed away a few hours ago at the age of 83 (born 30 June 1938 in Mashhad; died 25 May 2021 in London). May his dear memory be honoured.

Condolences to his daughter Saba,

We extend our condolences to the family of Esmail Khoi, to the Iranian artistic and cultural community in the Iranian Writers' Association "in Exile" and the Iranian PEN Association "in Exile", and to all his admirers and friends.

[https://m.soundcloud.com/khordadesabz/no0accftn5xz](https://m.soundcloud.com/khordadesabz/no0accftn5xz?fbclid=IwAR2z4pf4lWwb79PX_4BefKozwv3mxeZBUcvPHxuSfsX_TmHrA5n8NdPGlcc)

Esmail Khoi had been admitted to hospital on Friday, 21 May, suffering from severe pneumonia. Sadly, pulmonary, cardiac, and renal failure eventually reached a point where treatment was no longer possible.

And today we lost our esteemed and beloved poet.

Khoi's poems have been translated in various countries into English, Russian, French, German, Hindi, and Ukrainian. With his mastery of the English language, he also composed poetry in English and was the first Iranian poet to win the Rückert Prize in Coburg in 2010.

Following the 1979 Revolution, after a period of living in hiding, Khoi left Iran in 1984 and had lived in London ever since. He was also among the founders of the Iranian PEN Association in Exile and the Iranian Writers' Association in Exile. Since the 1979 Revolution, he had consistently been an opponent of the Islamic Republic regime.

Among his works are *Bi-Tab* (*Restless*), *Az Seday-e Sokhan-e Eshgh* (*From the Voice of Love's Speech*), *Dar Nabehangam* (*In the Untimely*), *Jahan-e Digari Miafarin-am* (*I Create Another World*), and *Ghahghah-e Nashenidani-ye Marg* (*The Unheard Laughter of Death*).

Several quatrains from Esmail Khoi's collection *The 1988 Massacre Aloud* (*Koshtar-e 67 be Bang-e Boland*):

I will not tell you what or how to write.

Of the inner state or of the outer world, write.

Write whatever surges forth from your heart,

O poet of the massacre, with blood write.

A thousand-year sorrow I carry in my heart.

Would that I might see no further grief of the heart.

I am a thousand years older today,

With the branding scar of thousands of youths upon my heart.

With all this blood that has flowed from its body,

Strength and vigour have departed from the limbs of the homeland.

Yet wait until there be torn from its moorings

The sheikh-toppling flood of young lives.

When that dragon-swine ascended to power,

A hundredfold worse in conduct than all the kings,

The chain of our existence became

Mourning upon mourning upon mourning upon mourning.

A sheikh whose head is filled with ignorance and superstition,

Whose art is the slaughter of the finest youths,

Strikes at our roots with the axe of his prayer:

May his own prayer break his back!

The fault-finding judge put a question to him:

— "Do you perform your prayers in every circumstance?"

He said nothing, and the judge had him executed:

Unaware that he was a Muslim, yet deaf and mute.

— "Do you rise for prayer?"

— "Day and night, with devotion!"

— "Do you curse your little faction?"

— "With a special curse!"

Yet he vomited at the question: "Your comrades—

Are you ready to fire the coup de grâce upon them too?"

O lover of humankind! What need have you of prayer?

Lo! Lift your head, like the Messiah, to the heights.

So divine is your love for the people,

That prayer itself ought to bow in prayer before you.

This slain one who sleeps upon the prison floor,

With the tulip that has blossomed upon his breast,

To the leaders of the party of hatred, sorrow, and death

Spoke of love, of joy, and of life.

This slain one who has fallen upon the ground

— Ever since his path led him into Evin —

Was a herald of freedom, yet

Fell into the clutches of the heralds of religion.

This slain one took seven or eight bullets, yet

By the coup de grâce he yielded up his soul, yet

With a smile upon his lips: for he had made his confession,

Yet had named not one of his comrades.

This slain one wished for no one to be killed,

Nor for anyone's hand to be stained with blood:

Behold his good fortune! That he fell before

Such heaps upon heaps of the slain were piled.

This slain one had a heart like the great hearts:

Ready to cast itself into the great sea:

The great sea of death swallowed him, yet

From him endures the hope of a better tomorrow.

.

Esmail Khoi was born on 30 June 1938 (9 Tir 1317) in the city of Mashhad. His father was financially comfortable, but suddenly fell into debt and lost his property; at just eight years of age, Esmail was forced to work in the bazaar during the summers to earn a living. Khoi was a child labourer, yet with the support of his maternal uncle he succeeded in continuing his education. After graduating from Daneshsaray-e Ali (the Higher Teachers' Training College), he travelled to Britain on a scholarship and earned a doctorate in philosophy from the University of London. Upon returning to Iran, he settled in Tehran and taught at Tarbiat Moallem University of Tehran. In an interview, Khoi stated that in Tehran he came under the influence of Mehdi Akhavan-Sales's *Zemestan* (*Winter*): "The book *Zemestan* awakened me and was my key to discovering modern poetry. Through *Zemestan*, I awoke from the eleven-hundred-year slumber of traditional poetry; after Akhavan, it was first and foremost Shamlou whom I came to know, and then gradually other poets. Nima Youshij was the last among the modernist poets whom I encountered at that time." Esmail Khoi was one of the founders of the Iranian Writers' Association and also served two terms on its executive board. Numerous collections of poetry have been published by him: *Bar Kheng-e Rahvar-e Zamin* (*Astride the Steed of the Earth*, 1967), *Bar Bam-e Gerdbad* (*Upon the Roof of the Whirlwind*, 1970), *Az Seday-e Sokhan-e Eshgh* (*From the Voice of Love's Speech*, 1970), *Faratar az Shab-e Aknounian* (*Beyond the Night of Our Contemporaries*, 1971), *Dar Nabehangam* (*In the Untimely*, 1984), *Gozareh-ye Hezareh* (*Millennium Proposition*, 1991), *Jahan-e Digari Miafarin-am* (*I Create Another World*, 2000), and *Sha'er-e Khalgham, Dahan-e Mihanam* (*I Am the Poet of My People, the Mouth of My Homeland*, 2000) are among his landmark works. Esmail Khoi's most recent poetry collection, *Dir Nemishavad Delam* (*My Heart Does Not Grow Late*), was published shortly before the poet's death by Zagros Publications in Atlanta, United States.

fr.title: Portrait de Masrour Makaremi et de son vin perse : Cyrhus
fr.executive_summary: https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/4ab4deaa56cf86414e1d38b405ea67ff003840002366-1920.jpg Laissez-moi vous conter une magnifique histoire autour d'un cépage planté dans le Bergeracois et qui, à la base, n'a rien à faire ici. Cette histoire,…
fr.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/4ab4deaa56cf86414e1d38b405ea67ff003840002366-1920.jpg

Laissez-moi vous conter une magnifique histoire autour d'un cépage planté dans le Bergeracois et qui, à la base, n'a rien à faire ici. Cette histoire, c'est bien plus que du vin : c'est l'histoire d'une famille, d'un homme et finalement d'une civilisation. Cyrhus Wine est une ode à l'Iran, le pays de naissance de Masrour Makaremi, pourfendeur de bonheur.

Cette histoire est née en Iran il y a plus de sept mille ans, berceau de la viticulture mondiale où ont été retrouvées des traces de rites et d'autres traditions liés au vin. L'occasion de penser que nous ne sommes finalement que très peu de chose dans l'Histoire.

Né dans la ville iranienne de Chiraz – nom tout trouvé – dans une famille engagée dans l'opposition politique aux mollahs afin de défendre leur liberté et leurs idéaux, Masrour Makaremi est arrivé en France à l'âge de 10 ans avec son père et sa sœur suite à la perte de sa mère, alors emprisonnée. Arrivé dans la douleur mais avec un regard neuf sur notre pays et notre manière de vivre, il s'oriente vers des études scientifiques puis devient spécialiste en orthopédie dento-faciale et orthodontie avant de venir s'installer il y a quelques années à Bergerac pour créer son propre cabinet. Avec également un bagage de neuroscientifique (excusez du peu !), il développe en parallèle de son cabinet une start-up dédiée au développement de technologies d'intelligence artificielle au service de la médecine.

## Quel rapport avec le vin ?

Les histoires liées au vin commencent toujours avec une rencontre. Pour Masrour, ce sera celle de son beau-père. Étant un grand amateur de vins et épicurien dans l'âme, il lui a fait découvrir de nouveaux horizons et, petit à petit, il a affiné ses goûts et son palais. Voulant rendre en quelque sorte à la France ce qu'elle lui a apporté dès son arrivée, une idée est née au fond de lui il y a presque 15 ans et a su germer tranquillement durant toutes ces années : marier ses deux cultures qui lui sont si chères, la Perse et sa France adoptive. Mais par quel moyen ? La vigne, bien sûr ! Et la création d'un vin totalement atypique, qui serait à lui seul le symbole parfait de ces deux mondes réunis dans un verre, à l'unisson du battement de cœur de l'Homme. Une sorte de renaissance historique en hommage à la plus vieille région viticole de l'Humanité.

Voici comment est tout naturellement née l'idée de Cyrhus. Le nom tout d'abord : Cyrhus, en hommage à Cyrus le Grand, célèbre et grand roi perse, et avec un H en guise de clin d'œil au cépage Shiraz.
En association avec Grégory Dubard (Vignobles Dubard), il a décidé de planter deux hectares de Shiraz en 2016. N'ayant comme seul but pour cette première cuvée que la recherche du meilleur, Masrour et Grégory ont laissé le temps faire son œuvre et c'est avec la récolte 2019 que seules 559 bouteilles seront vendues uniquement via le site internet [www.cyrhus-wine.com](https://www.cyrhus-wine.com/) en juin prochain. Le nombre de 559 n'ayant pas été choisi au hasard, il s'agit là encore d'un clin d'œil à la date du début de l'Empire perse, né en -559 avant notre ère et mené par Cyrus le Grand. Ne nous trompons pas : il ne s'agit pas là d'une ultime niche marketing destinée à faire prendre de la valeur à des bouteilles en série ultra-limitée. Non, la démarche de Masrour, pour avoir passé une journée en sa compagnie et celle de ses proches afin de m'expliquer son histoire et celle de son vin, n'a pour autre visée qu'une utopie rare en ces temps un peu troublés : le partage et la reconnaissance de deux mondes réunis par le vin.

Jamais très loin de lui, son père, Hassan, psychanalyste mais aussi artiste et poète ayant exposé à l'UNESCO et militant des Droits de l'Homme, est un homme bienveillant. Il suffit de croiser son regard pétillant pour comprendre la gentillesse et l'humilité qui l'animent. À eux deux, on comprend ce que le mot humilité signifie.

L'idée de planter de la Shiraz au milieu d'une appellation plutôt habituée au merlot ou au cabernet sauvignon n'est pas dénuée de sens. Tout d'abord parce que le type de sol argilo-calcaire et graveleux de la région est plutôt propice au développement de ce cépage, et d'autre part parce que c'est une région qui est assez ouverte aux essais hors cadre et hors cahiers des charges traditionnels. C'est donc tout un symbole que d'avoir planté cette vigne à cet endroit-là.

https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/6137f750ebbb8a83c880bb648aef2c7b-1920.jpg
Masrour et ses amphores

L'autre idée de Masrour, non content de créer un vin aux symboles multiculturels, a été de recréer le goût des vins perses de sa région natale comme au temps de Cyrus le Grand. Afin de se rapprocher au maximum des standards de l'époque, il a fait vieillir son vin uniquement dans des amphores en terre, poussant le détail des arômes les plus authentiques de l'époque en faisant produire des amphores avec une température de cuisson modérée. En effet, une amphore est ni plus ni moins une poterie, très technique certes dans sa réalisation, mais qui nécessite une chauffe pour cuire la terre. Tout comme pour les barriques en bois, il est possible de choisir son type de cuisson mais pas du tout pour les mêmes raisons. Autant avec une barrique, on cherche à rendre le vin plus ou moins tannique, plus ou moins vanillé, fumé et j'en passe, autant avec une amphore, la pièce de terre cuite ne va pas apporter d'arômes particuliers en elle-même, mais c'est l'échange avec l'oxygène qui va rendre le vin qui y vieillit plus ou moins fruité, plus ou moins oxydatif. Plus l'amphore est cuite à forte température, moins elle sera poreuse et plus l'échange avec l'oxygène sera réduit. En revanche, comme l'a fait Masrour avec ses amphores, moins forte sera la température de cuisson, plus la terre sera poreuse et donc plus l'échange avec l'oxygène sera grand, et c'est là toute la difficulté des choix que doit faire un vigneron dans l'optique du vin qu'il souhaite produire. Rien n'est donc laissé au hasard pour la création de ces quelque 559 premières bouteilles.

Si vous êtes l'un des heureux futurs acquéreurs d'une bouteille de Cyrhus, je ne peux que vous conseiller ces deux recettes que nous avons réalisées avec Sandie, la femme de Masrour, et le beau-père de ce dernier.

### Le Tahdig

Littéralement « fond de casserole », c'est un plat typiquement iranien à base de riz safrané avec une croûte bien croustillante sur le dessus qui demande malgré tout un peu de technicité pour arriver à un tel résultat. Le riz se cuit à l'étouffée pendant une heure, formant ainsi une croûte dorée au fond du faitout. Pas de secret dans la cuisine à travers le monde : du beurre pour décoller facilement et donner un croquant incomparable à cette sorte de gâteau de riz croustillant. C'est délicieux avec le goût du safran incomparable.
Afin de rester sur le thème du mariage des cultures, accompagnez-le comme j'ai pu le déguster, avec de belles tranches de magret de canard du Périgord.

https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/380ca04cd75dfb2a6c829b5451d1d008-1920.jpg
Le Tahdig

## Le riz à l'iranienne

Avec une cuisson en cocotte, là encore du safran. Rien de bien compliqué. Mais tout réside dans le dressage, aussi joli que coloré et avec une explosion de saveurs. Placez votre riz en dôme au centre d'un plat rond. Rajoutez par-dessus des grenades, des amandes, des pistaches torréfiées et concassées ; faites des petits tas, tout autour par-dessus le dôme de riz, laissez libre cours à votre imagination pour faire des motifs.

## Faites la rencontre de Masrour, le vendredi 11 juin à 19h

Toutlevin vous invite à rencontrer Masrour Makaremi à travers son premier webinaire. Notre rédactrice en chef Charlotte, accompagnée de Masrour, va vous transporter au cœur même de la naissance du vin, de sa culture dans la Perse antique à son renouveau avec le vin Cyrhus. Afin d'en apprendre davantage sur cette culture millénaire, nous vous donnons rendez-vous le vendredi 11 juin à 19h.
Pour y participer, rien de plus simple : inscrivez-vous ci-dessous !

[https://www.toutlevin.com/article/portrait-de-masrour-makaremi-et-de-son-vin-perse-cyrhus?fbclid=IwAR3Zy_sWttS_UR5b67ZZ5-ZxWhRLaWD410VLpKJ9sAl7y4RZvgp9r1J91SU](https://www.toutlevin.com/article/portrait-de-masrour-makaremi-et-de-son-vin-perse-cyrhus?fbclid=IwAR3Zy_sWttS_UR5b67ZZ5-ZxWhRLaWD410VLpKJ9sAl7y4RZvgp9r1J91SU)

en.title: Portrait of Masrour Makaremi and His Persian Wine: Cyrhus
en.executive_summary: https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/4ab4deaa56cf86414e1d38b405ea67ff003840002366-1920.jpg Let me tell you a wonderful story about a grape variety planted in the Bergerac region that, on the face of it, had no business being there. This story,…
en.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/4ab4deaa56cf86414e1d38b405ea67ff003840002366-1920.jpg

Let me tell you a wonderful story about a grape variety planted in the Bergerac region that, on the face of it, had no business being there. This story is about far more than wine; it is the story of a family, of a man, and ultimately of a civilisation: Cyrhus Wine is an ode to Iran, the birthplace of Masrour Makaremi, a true champion of happiness.

This story began in Iran more than seven thousand years ago, the cradle of world viticulture, where traces of rituals and other traditions linked to wine have been discovered. It is a fitting occasion to reflect on how small we ultimately are within History.

Born in the Iranian city of Shiraz — a name that could scarcely be more apt — into a family engaged in political opposition to the mullahs in order to defend their freedom and ideals, Masrour Makaremi arrived in France at the age of ten with his father and sister following the loss of his mother, who was then imprisoned. Arriving amidst sorrow, yet with a fresh perspective on our country and our way of life, he turned towards scientific studies and became a specialist in dentofacial orthopaedics and orthodontics before settling in Bergerac a few years ago to establish his own practice. Also possessing a background as a neuroscientist (no small feat!), he is simultaneously developing, alongside his practice, a start-up dedicated to artificial intelligence technologies in the service of medicine.

## What Connection to Wine?

Stories about wine always begin with an encounter. For Masrour, it was his father-in-law. A great wine enthusiast and an epicurean at heart, he introduced Masrour to new horizons and, little by little, refined his tastes and palate. Wishing in some way to give back to France what it had offered him from the moment of his arrival, an idea took root deep within him nearly fifteen years ago and quietly germinated over all those years: to unite the two cultures so dear to him — Persia and his adoptive France. Yet by what means? The vine, of course! And the creation of an utterly atypical wine that would stand in itself as the perfect symbol of these two worlds brought together in a glass, beating in unison with the human heart. A kind of historical renaissance in homage to the oldest wine-growing region of humanity.

Thus was the idea of Cyrhus quite naturally born. First, the name: Cyrhus, in homage to Cyrus the Great, the celebrated and mighty Persian king, with an "H" added as a subtle nod to the Shiraz grape variety.
In partnership with Grégory Dubard (Vignobles Dubard), he decided to plant two hectares of Shiraz in 2016. With no other aim for this inaugural vintage than the pursuit of excellence, Masrour and Grégory allowed time to do its work, and it is from the 2019 harvest that just 559 bottles will be sold exclusively via the website [www.cyrhus-wine.com](https://www.cyrhus-wine.com/) this coming June. The figure 559 was not chosen at random; it too is a reference to the founding date of the Persian Empire, born in 559 BCE and led by Cyrus the Great. Make no mistake: this is not some ultimate marketing niche designed to inflate the value of ultra-limited-edition bottles. No — having spent a day in Masrour's company and that of his loved ones so he could explain his story and that of his wine to me, his endeavour has no other aim than a rare utopia in these somewhat troubled times: the sharing and mutual recognition of two worlds united through wine.

Never far from his side, his father, Hassan — a psychoanalyst, as well as an artist and poet who has exhibited at UNESCO, and a human rights advocate — is a profoundly benevolent man. One need only meet his sparkling gaze to understand the kindness and humility that animate him. Between the two of them, one truly grasps what the word humility means.

The idea of planting Shiraz in the heart of an appellation more accustomed to Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon is by no means devoid of sense. First, because the clay-limestone and gravelly soil of the region is rather well suited to the development of this grape variety; and second, because it is a region quite open to experimentation outside traditional frameworks and specifications. Planting this vineyard in this very place is therefore deeply symbolic.

https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/6137f750ebbb8a83c880bb648aef2c7b-1920.jpg
Masrour and his amphorae

Masrour's other idea — not content with merely creating a wine rich in multicultural symbols — was to recreate the taste of the Persian wines of his native region as they were in the time of Cyrus the Great. To come as close as possible to the standards of that era, he aged his wine exclusively in earthenware amphorae, pushing the pursuit of the most authentic aromas of antiquity so far as to have amphorae produced at a moderate firing temperature. Indeed, an amphora is nothing more and nothing less than pottery — highly technical in its craftsmanship, to be sure, yet requiring firing to bake the clay. Just as with wooden barrels, one can choose the type of firing, though for entirely different reasons. Whereas with a barrel one seeks to make the wine more or less tannic, more or less vanilla-scented, smoky, and so forth, with an amphora the terracotta vessel does not impart particular aromas of its own; rather, it is the exchange with oxygen that renders the wine ageing within it more or less fruity, more or less oxidative. The higher the temperature at which the amphora is fired, the less porous it will be and the more limited the oxygen exchange. Conversely, as Masrour has done with his amphorae, the lower the firing temperature, the more porous the clay will be and thus the greater the exchange with oxygen — therein lies the full complexity of the choices a winemaker must make with regard to the wine they wish to produce. Nothing, therefore, has been left to chance in the crafting of these first 559 bottles.

If you are among the fortunate future buyers of a bottle of Cyrhus, I can only recommend these two recipes that we prepared together with Sandie, Masrour's wife, and his father-in-law.

### Tahdig

Literally "bottom of the pot", this is a quintessential Iranian dish based on saffron rice with a wonderfully crisp crust on top, which nevertheless requires a measure of culinary skill to achieve such a result. The rice is steamed covered for an hour, thereby forming a golden crust at the bottom of the heavy pot. There is no secret in cuisines across the world: butter to release it effortlessly and lend an unrivalled crunch to this sort of crispy rice cake. It is delicious, with the incomparable flavour of saffron.
To stay true to the theme of the marriage of cultures, serve it, just as I had the pleasure of tasting it, alongside generous slices of Périgord duck breast (magret).

https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/380ca04cd75dfb2a6c829b5451d1d008-1920.jpg
Tahdig

## Iranian-Style Rice

Cooked in a casserole pot, once again with saffron. Nothing overly complicated. Yet everything lies in the plating, as attractive as it is colourful, offering an explosion of flavours. Shape your rice into a dome in the centre of a round platter. Add pomegranate seeds, almonds, and roasted, crushed pistachios on top; arrange them in small clusters all around over the dome of rice, and give free rein to your imagination to create decorative patterns.

## Meet Masrour on Friday, 11 June at 7:00 p.m.

Toutlevin invites you to meet Masrour Makaremi through its very first webinar. Our editor-in-chief, Charlotte, accompanied by Masrour, will transport you to the very heart of the birth of wine, from its culture in ancient Persia to its renewal with Cyrhus wine. To learn more about this millennia-old culture, join us on Friday, 11 June at 7:00 p.m.
To take part, nothing could be simpler — register below!

fr.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/10-%DA%98%D9%88%D8%A6%D9%86-2021.jpg

Dédié aux centaines d'êtres nobles et de compagnons qui, au cours du dernier demi-siècle, sont partis pour honorer la dignité humaine et ne sont jamais revenus.

Mais il n'est pas venu…

Il a dit et redit…

Quand j'aurai lavé toute la vaisselle, je viendrai…

Il a dit et redit…

Quand j'aurai fermé toutes les portes, je viendrai…

Nous avons eu beau attendre, il n'est pas venu.

Toute la vaisselle était propre et toutes les portes étaient fermées,

Mais il n'est pas venu…

Ceux qui dorment dans les cartons,

Ceux qui dorment dans les tombes,

Les qalandars sans lieu ni demeure,

Les amoureux éperdus et passionnés :

Ils n'ont ni vaisselle ni porte.

On eût dit qu'il est parti cette nuit-là, au bout de cette nuit-là il est parti :

Pour devenir le vase de ceux qui n'ont point de vaisselle,

Pour devenir la porte de ceux qui n'ont point de porte.

Sa voix s'élève encore de la cuisine, à la fin de chaque nuit :

Quand j'aurai lavé toute la vaisselle,

Quand j'aurai fermé toutes les portes,

Je viendrai.

Hassan Makaremi

France, printemps 2021

Ma fille, Chowra Khanom, m'a fait un cadeau : elle a traduit ce poème et m'a comblé de joie.

Ma fille Chowra Khanom m’a fait un cadeau elle a traduit ce poème.

Mais il n'est pas venu

Il dit et dit encore

Quand j'aurai lavé toute la vaisselle, je viendrai

Il dit et dit encore

Quand j'aurai fermé toutes les portes, je viendrai

Nous n'avons cessé d'attendre, mais il n'est pas venu

Toute la vaisselle était faite et toutes les portes fermées,

Mais il n'est pas venu

Ceux qui dorment dans les cartons

Ceux qui dorment dans les tombes

Les Qalandars sans lieux ni espaces

Les Amoureux et les passionnés

N'ont ni vaisselles ni portes

Il semble que cette nuit-là est passée ; à la nuit passée, il est parti

Pour devenir la vaisselles des gens sans vaisselle

Pour devenir la porte des sans portes

Dans la cuisine, au fond de chaque nuit, on peut encore entendre sa voix

Quand j'aurai lavé toute la vaisselle,

Quand j'aurai fermé toutes les portes,

Je viendrai.

Makaremi

France, printemps 2021

en.body_markdown:
https://www.makaremi.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/10-%DA%98%D9%88%D8%A6%D9%86-2021.jpg

Dedicated to the hundreds of noble human beings and companions who, over the past half-century, departed to honour human dignity and never returned.

But he did not come…

He said, and said again…

Once I have washed all the dishes, I will come…

He said, and said again…

Once I have closed all the doors, I will come…

However long we waited, he did not come.

The dishes were all clean and the doors were all closed,

But he did not come…

Those who sleep in cardboard boxes,

Those who sleep in graves,

The wandering qalandars with neither place nor abode,

The enraptured and lovelorn lovers:

They have neither dish nor door.

It seemed he departed that night, at the end of that night he departed:

To become the vessel of those without vessels,

To become the door of those without doors.

His voice still drifts from the kitchen at the close of every night:

Once I have washed all the dishes,

Once I have closed all the doors,

I will come.

Hassan Makaremi

France, Spring 2021

My daughter, Chowra Khanom, gave me a gift: she translated this poem and filled me with joy.

My daughter Chowra Khanom gave me a gift; she translated this poem.

But he did not come

He says and says again

When I have washed all the dishes, I will come

He says and says again

When I have closed all the doors, I will come

We never ceased waiting, yet he did not come

All the dishes were done and all the doors closed,

But he did not come

Those who sleep in cardboard boxes

Those who sleep in graves

The Qalandars without places or spaces

The Lovers and the impassioned

Have neither dishes nor doors

It seems that night has passed; at the passing of the night, he departed

To become the dishes of those without dishes

To become the door of those without doors

In the kitchen, in the depths of every night, one can still hear his voice

When I have washed all the dishes,

When I have closed all the doors,

I will come.

Makaremi

France, Spring 2021
